transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a little trouble staying on track with things. I mean, I know everyone gets distracted sometimes, right? So I don't want to make a huge deal out of it or anything. 

But the main thing is, I just kind of get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. Like, I’ll be sitting down, really trying to work on a job application, and then... I don't know, a car drives by outside, or my phone lights up, or some random idea just pops into my head. And before I even notice what's happening, I've completely wandered off and I'm doing something else entirely. 

Is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and giving you the information you need.
Did you have similar trouble with attention or staying on task when you were a child?

Well, um, I guess so, yeah. But I mean, wasn't every kid a little bit like that? I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I really tried my best to be good. 

But, um... yeah, even back in elementary school, my teachers were always having to move my seat. I guess I just... I had a habit of talking out of turn sometimes. And, well, I did forget my homework a lot, which I always felt terrible about. And when we had worksheets, I'd kind of rush through them and make some silly, careless mistakes. 

I just had a lot of energy, you know? And I wanted to get things done quickly. I hope that makes sense. Is that the sort of childhood stuff you're looking for? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier or anything like that. 

I guess I get a little stressed sometimes, like when I'm trying to figure out the job stuff, but... well, that's pretty normal, right? Everyone gets a little stressed about things like that. But I don't just sit around worrying about nothing, if that's what you mean. I try to stay pretty positive and just kind of take things as they come. 

Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have days where I feel a little bummed out if I didn't get much done, but I don't feel depressed. I try to keep a good attitude, you know? Just kind of keep moving forward. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all day. I'm generally a pretty upbeat guy. Is that... is that helpful? I hope I'm not making things too complicated.
How much does this difficulty with attention interfere with your day-to-day life?

Well, um... I guess it gets in the way a little bit, but I don't want to make it sound like I can't function or anything. I mean, I'm trying really hard. 

It's just, well... I really want to be an automotive technician. I'm great at the hands-on stuff, I promise you that. But, um, I've had some trouble with the paperwork side of things. I've missed a few training deadlines, and... well, I've had to redo some applications because I missed some details. So I guess I'm not really moving forward with it as fast as I'd like. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly. I don't want you to think I'm lazy, because I really do want to work. It's just hard to keep all the dates and forms straight sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you still have trouble being fidgety or unable to sit still when you need to stay seated?

Um, well, I guess I do move around a bit, but I wouldn't say I'm, like, bouncing off the walls or anything disruptive. I try really hard to be polite and pay attention when I'm sitting with someone. 

But, uh, I guess if you really watched me... my leg is usually bouncing a little. Or I might be, you know, clicking a pen or just kind of messing with my keys in my pocket. I honestly don't even realize I'm doing it most of the time until someone points it out. It's just a nervous habit, I think. A lot of people do that, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing. Is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
Did these attention or restlessness problems happen in more than one setting, like both at school and at home, when you were growing up?

Yeah, um... I guess it was kind of everywhere. I mean, my parents definitely noticed it at home, but school was... well, I guess school was a bit of a struggle. I really liked my teachers, I promise I wasn't trying to be a troublemaker or anything. But, um, even way back in elementary school, they were kind of always having to move my seat around the classroom. 

I guess I just got a little too eager sometimes and would talk out of turn. And, uh, I'd forget to bring my homework in, even when I really meant to do it. Plus, whenever we had worksheets, I'd just kind of rush through them because I wanted to be finished, but then I'd end up making all these silly, careless mistakes. 

I feel bad looking back on it, honestly, because I know I must have been a handful for them. I really was trying my best to be a good student, though. Is that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
